title: Theo Rossi, Ron Perlman & Rachelle Goulding Wrap Under-The-Radar Horror Film ‘Renew’, First Look Revealed
full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Tradition Pictures Sets Multi-Project Partnership With Kenan Thompson’s Artists For Artists; Mark Canton, James Maslow & Joseph Sikora Join Advisory Board Meridian Pictures Picks Up Mike Maples Western ‘The Regulator’ Rhys Ifans, Lily Rabe & Sarah Catherine Hook Dramedy ‘Capsized’ Boarded By The Yellow Affair Ahead Of U.S. Festival Bow View All October 7, 2026 9:10am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: Theo Rossi, Ron Perlman and Rachelle Goulding Penske Media EXCLUSIVE : Theo Rossi has added an under-the-radar horror film to his genre era in the shape of Renew , which will reunite him on screen with his Sons Of Anarchy , Come With Me and The Saviors co-star Ron Perlman . Filming recently wrapped on Renew , “a suspense-driven horror film that begins as an intimate love story before descending into visceral horror”. Directed by Tommy DeNucci from a screenplay he co-wrote with Rossi, the film, which also stars Rachelle Goulding ( Suits LA ), “follows a husband and wife who return to the secluded Montana guest ranch where they were married to renew their vows, hoping to leave the past behind and begin again. But when she mysteriously disappears, he is forced to confront the life he fought to escape as he uncovers a hidden evil lurking beneath the ranch’s idyllic façade.” Below is a first-look image. Related Stories News Ron Perlman, Peter Facinelli, Mark Elias & Serena Wang Starring In Indie Film 'We Could Be Heroes' News Ron Perlman, Shohreh Aghdashloo & Cuba Gooding Jr. Set For Golden Dunes Jury Duty In Dubai The ensemble cast also includes Ronnie Gene Blevins, Allison Dunbar, Sam Daly, Danny Rivera, Rebecca Creskoff, Darko Ostojic, Bonnie Gayle Sparks, Barron Boedecker and Chris Wilks. Diana Hull and Rossi produced the film. Watch on Deadline Production wrapped in Red Lodge and Roberts, Montana. Rossi was joined on the project by longtime producing partner Nicholas Carmona. DeNucci has previously directed Rossi in movies Vault and Play Dirty . Rossi, also known for HBO’s The Penguin , Netflix’s Carry-On , and Emily the Criminal , commented: “What excited Tommy and me most was building the film around two people with a shared history who are trying to find their way back to each other. There’s hope, humor and heart in that, but also the weight of everything they’ve been through. When that hope comes under threat, you find out how far someone will go for the person they love. We wanted audiences invested in Randy and Liz from the very beginning, so they feel the danger right alongside them.” Producer Diana Hull said: “Watching this cast and crew bring Renew to life in Montana was incredibly rewarding. The film asks a great deal of its performers, both emotionally and physically, and their commitment carried through every stage of production. We can’t wait for audiences to experience what we’ve created together.” DeNucci added: “From the very first draft, we wanted audiences to settle into this beautiful Montana escape and genuinely fall in love with Randy and Liz. The more authentic their relationship feels, the more terrifying it becomes when everything begins to unravel. This remarkable cast brought that emotional journey to life in ways that exceeded every expectation.” Rossie and Perlman will also join forces on the upcoming Sons of Anarchy reboot Legends . title: ‘SNL’ Alum Punkie Johnson Sets Debut Stand-Up Special ‘Long Tiddie Short Story’ With Hartbeat
full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt David Krumholtz Joins ‘The Trial Of Louise Woodward’ At HBO After Mulling “Indefinite Break” From Acting Ben Shapiro Decries Suspension Of Production On Daily Wire Movie ‘Pawn Shop’ As Shoot Resumes: “Politics, Pure And Simple” Jessica Biel Joins Searchlight Pictures’ ‘Playmates’ View All October 7, 2026 9:06am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Punkie Johnson Van Corona EXCLUSIVE: Former Saturday Night Live cast member Punkie Johnson has announced that her debut stand-up special, Long Tiddie Short Story , will premiere on Hartbeat’s LOL Stand-Up YouTube Channel October 21st. In the special, Johnson steps into the ring to reflect on her time at SNL , her complicated relationship with queerness, and her own questionable life choices. It’s billed as a brutally honest and unfiltered hour about marriage, sex, drugs, and what can transpire when you pretend to be “normal.” Johnson taped the hour at The Comedy Store in Los Angeles. Directed by Steven Feinartz, it’ll be available as a comedy album across audio streaming services on November 13, available for pre-order on October 21. The special is produced by Feinartz and Danielle Lee and exec produced by Johnson, Ethan Stern and Dominic Del Bene. Related Stories Casting 'Barbershop': Roy Wood Jr., Punkie Johnson, Brett Gray & E.J. Bonilla Join Jermaine Fowler In Amazon Series News Punkie Johnson & Chloe Troast Talk "Very Hard" Post-'SNL' Careers: "No Life Jacket" Hartbeat reunites with Johnson after producing her 2023 SiriusXM show, Love Thang , for Kevin Hart’s LOL Radio. Recently, she’s also filmed a role in their upcoming Barbershop TV series for Prime Video. The special joins a growing stand-up slate from Hartbeat, including the second installment of LOL Live at Hulu, with new half-hour specials currently rolling out monthly, as well as Funny AF , the stand-up competition series that was picked up for a second season after drumming up major viewership at Netflix. Watch on Deadline The deal to distribute Johnson’s special was spearheaded by Hartbeat President & Chief Distribution Officer Jeff Clanagan and VP, Comedy Eric Weil. Clanagan told us, “Punkie is exactly the kind of singular comedic voice we want to champion at Hartbeat. We’ve had the opportunity to work with her across radio, television and now stand-up, and bringing her debut special directly to audiences on YouTube reflects our larger strategy of creating more ways for great comedians to reach fans wherever they are. We’re excited to continue building with Punkie and supporting her work across platforms.” Weil added, “Punkie has the rare ability to be completely fearless and deeply personal at the same time. Long Tiddie Short Story is unmistakably her — honest, unpredictable and incredibly funny. We’re proud to be part of her first stand-up special and to continue a creative relationship with Punkie that has grown across radio, television and stand-up.” A comedian, actress and writer from New Orleans, Louisiana, Johnson was with SNL for four seasons beginning in 2020. Touring nationally these days while developing original television and film projects, she’s previously been seen starring in two seasons of Lena Waithe’s The Chi , with additional roles in HBO Max’s Love Life , Netflix’s Space Force , HBO’s A Black Lady Sketch Show and CBS’s Ghosts . Johnson also served as a writer/consultant on Peacock’s reboot of Queer as Folk and appeared in the cult hit comedy film Bottoms opposite Ayo Edebiri and Rachel Sennott. She is repped by Ethan Stern at Underscore, WME and Ziffren Brittenham. title: ‘The Hunting Wives’ Lands Early Season 3 Renewal at Netflix
full_text: Skip to main content By Jackie Strause Plus Icon Jackie Strause Managing Editor, East Coast jackiedstrause Follow Sign Up View All October 7, 2026 9:00am Malin Akerman and Brittany Snow in 'The Hunting Wives' season one. Kent Smith/Netflix Logo text The Hunting Wives have hit their mark — and landed an early renewal. The Netflix series from Rebecca Cutter starring Malin Akerman and Brittany Snow , who lead a cutthroat yet soapy set of Texas housewives, has nabbed a season three renewal ahead of season two’s return. Season two, which was announced in September, returns Thanksgiving Day (Nov. 26) with the original (surviving) cast reprising their roles. The third season will be another eight episodes, with a release date and cast yet to be announced. Related Stories Movies Ava DuVernay Returns With One of Netflix's Most Political Docs Ever: "This Movie Kicked My Butt" TV Jamie Foxx Does Not Want to Be Canceled Over New Hulu Stand-up Special: "After That Kevin Hart Roast, I Had to Cut Everything" The Hunting Wives , adapted by showrunner Cutter from the bestselling novel of the same name by May Cobb, became a 2025 summer sensation for Netflix when it released season one . “I’m so stoked to be heading back to Maple Brook, and I promise that once you’ve finished season two, you’ll be desperate to see what happens next. Buckle up, because season three will be even more scandalous and twisted,” Cutter said on Wednesday in a statement about the early renewal. Cutter’s statement implies that similar to season one , season two could also end on a cliffhanger. ( Snow has already teased a big death to come.) The sexy and binge-y thriller, which was originally developed for Starz, is a Lionsgate Television and 3 Arts Entertainment production and will release both season two and three on the streamer as a Netflix-branded series. Producers pivoted the series to Netflix in the lead up to Starz’s official split from Lionsgate and released The Hunting Wives weeks later, on July 21. It became the most-viewed streaming series in the U.S. and spent six weeks in Nielsen’s top 10 chart of streaming originals. Created by writer/showrunner/EP Cutter ( Hightown ), Hunting Wives is also executive produced by Erwin Stoff for 3 Arts Entertainment and Cobb. THR

title: ‘Anna Pigeon’ Renewed for Second Season on USA
full_text: Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All October 7, 2026 9:00am Tracy Spiridakos (center) as the title character in USA's 'Anna Pigeon.' Michelle Faye/USA Network Logo text USA Network ‘s rebuild of a scripted series roster continues with the renewal of Anna Pigeon . The cable outlet has picked up a second season of the show, which stars Tracy Spiridakos ( Chicago PD ) as a crime-solving national park ranger. The renewal for Anna Pigeon , which is based on a series of novels by Nevada Barr, comes two days before its Oct. 9 season finale. “It’s been really thrilling to see audiences fall in love with Anna and come to the park every week,” showrunner Morwyn Brebner said in a release announcing the renewal. “We’re so grateful to our cast and crew who brought Nevada Barr’s iconic world to life with such heart and passion; we cannot wait to get back outside for season two.” Related Stories TV Why Now Was the Time for Golf Channel to Revive 'Big Break' TV Medical Drama 'Diplomatic Immunity' Scores USA Series Order Produced by Cineflix and Seven24 Films, Anna Pigeon has drawn decent ratings for USA: Its series premiere drew 2.35 million viewers over seven days, making it the best debut for a USA scripted show since 2018. The show is the No. 1 new scripted drama on ad-supported cable for the year so far. “ Anna Pigeon has connected with audiences in a meaningful way, bringing a compelling new heroine and a fresh perspective to USA Network,” said Michael Sluchan, senior vp scripted content for Versant Entertainment. “We’re thrilled to continue Anna’s journey with Tracy, Morwyn, [director and executive producer Lea Thompson] and our incredible partners at Cineflix.” The Versant-owned USA is slowly building up a slate of scripted series that harken back to the network’s “blue skies” era of the 2000s and 2010s (under NBCUniversal). Along with Anna Pigeon , USA has the John Grisham legal drama The Rainmaker — whose second season premieres Oct. 16 — and the recently ordered Diplomatic Immunity , about a doctor assigned to the U.S. embassy in Rome. Brebner ( Rookie Blue, Crew Girl ) and Thompson executive produce Anna Pigeon with Brett Burlock, Sonia Hosko, Todd Berger, Julie Di Cresce, Tom Cox, Jordy Randall, Peter Emerson and Gordon Gilbertson. Leslie Cowan serves as producer. THR

title: Creator Maurice Kamara Signs With UTA (Exclusive)
full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 7, 2026 9:00am Maurice Kamara Courtesy of UTA Maurice Kamara, the cultural tastemaker behind The People Gallery online fashion page, has signed with United Talent Agency for representation . The People Gallery features man-on-the-street style interviews with celebrities like Oprah Winfrey, Pamela Anderson and Michael B. Jordan at fashion shows and other events or just New Yorkers showing their street style when out and about. “Let’s see your fit, describe it for us,” Kamara will often say from behind the camera as he opens the celebrity encounters. Leveraging over 3 million followers across TikTok and Instagram, The People Gallery also increasingly offers an online voice for brands Kamara partners with. “What began as Kamara stopping stylish strangers on the streets of New York has grown into a global platform documenting the people, personalities, and perspectives shaping culture across fashion, music, sports, and beyond,” the agency said in a statement. The UTA Creators division will expand Kamara’s opportunities in digital media, brand partnerships, sports and other platforms. The signing comes as Kamara builds on his brand partnerships and high-profile appearances, including an upcoming collaboration with UGG and a cameo in Drake’s recently released short film FOMO. Brooklyn native Kamara after over 15 years in high end retail also now attends Met Gala and fashion weeks around the world and is the subject of New York Times and GQ profiles. UTA was early to the creators game, launching a dedicated digital talent group in 2006 to identify and represent category-leading creators across emerging and established platforms. THR

title: Julio Peña Joins Josh Heuston, Nicole Wallace in Amazon MGM’s ‘Throttled’
full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexy Perez Plus Icon Lexy Perez Senior Digital Editor and Producer View All October 7, 2026 9:00am Julio Peña, Nicole Wallace and Josh Heuston Isaac Morell; Pablo Curto; Aurore Marechal/Getty Images Julio Peña has joined the cast of Amazon MGM Studios ‘ Throttled , an upcoming film based on the book from Lauren Ashers’ Dirty Air series. The actor joins previously announced stars Nicole Wallace (the Culpa Mia trilogy) and Josh Heuston ( Off Campus ). In the upcoming romance from Amazon MGM Studios, Peña will play Santi Alatorre, “the older brother of Maya Alatorre (portrayed by Wallace) and a driver on the racing circuit whose teammate and fiercest rival, Noah Slade (Heuston), falls into a forbidden romance with Maya.“ Related Stories TV Peacock's 'The Good Daughter' Trailer: Rose Byrne, Meghann Fahy Attempt to Solve Small-Town Murder in Suspenseful Thriller Series TV Inside the Shocking Decision to End 'Young Sheldon' at Its Peak (Exclusive Excerpt) The trio shared a social media post to announce Peña‘s casting. In their video, Wallace and Heuston are seen talking privately, only for Peña to interrupt and squeeze in the middle of them. “Welcome to the team,” Heuston says to Peña, only for Peña to shake his hand and respond, “Thanks! Just stay away from my sister.“ He then hugs Wallace while Heuston laughs it off saying, “You bet!“ Melissa Osborne ( My Fault: London , My Oxford Year ) will adapt the script and Nzingha Stewart ( Daisy Jones & the Six ) is set to direct. Max Handelman and Elizabeth Banks of Brownstone Productions are producing along with Ethea Entertainment’s Jennifer Gibgot and Andrew Panay, who recently produced The Last Sunrise , Prime’s film adaptation of Anna Todd‘s bestselling romance novel. Garrett Grant is also producing, with Alison Small of Brownstone Productions and Asher executive producing. Asher‘s 2020 book Throttled is the first of four books in the Dirty Air sports romance series. The adaptation marks another addition to Amazon MGM‘s building library of book-to-screen adaptations , including Off Campus , Every Year After and The Love Hypothesis. Peña is best known for his work in the Through My Window t rilogy on Netflix, whose first installment logged 68 million views in its first two weeks. He recently wrapped the untitled Meta series based on A24’s Talk to Me . Last year he starred in The Captive, which premiered at TIFF and earned him a Goya Award nomination for best new actor. Peña also stars in the Money Heist Netflix spinoff Berlin . Peña is represented by Anonymous Content, YouRock Talent Partners, and Jackoway Austen Tyerman Wertheimer Mandelbaum Morris Bernstein Trattner Auerbach Hynick Jaime LeVine Sample & Klein. THR

title: Oscars: Saudi Arabia Picks ‘A Matter of Life and Death’ as Best Int’l Feature Submission
full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All October 7, 2026 9:00am 'A Matter of Life and Death' Courtesy of Front Row The Saudi Film Commission has selected Anas Ba Tahaf‘s A Matter of Life and Death as Saudi Arabia’s official submission for the best international feature film Oscar category at the 99th Academy Awards. Written by and starring Sarah Taibah alongside Yaqoub Al Farhan, the film is produced by Film Clinic, Front Row Filmed Entertainment and Arabia Pictures, with Front Row handling international sales. The film is set in contemporary Jeddah and blends romance, fantasy and black comedy in a highly stylized visual world. “At heart, it is a love story, just not the safe kind,” a description of the movie notes. “At its center is Hayat, a fiercely independent young woman convinced that a generational curse will kill her on her 30th birthday. Having made peace with dying, she crosses paths with Yousef, a brilliant but emotionally detached heart surgeon living with bradycardia. His abnormally slow heartbeat only seems to quicken when he comes close to death – or to killing. As a surgeon surrounded every day by the fragile line between life and death, temptation is never far away.” So, while she wants to die, he wants to kill, but inconveniently, they fall in love with each other. “Hayat is impulsive, funny, stubborn, fearless and spectacularly headstrong, a contemporary Saudi woman written without explanation or apology,” says Front Row. “Her independence is not the story. It is simply who she is.” Related Stories Movies Saoirse Ronan Responds to Rumors That Husband Jack Lowden Will Be the Next James Bond TV BBC Releases 'Blue Planet III' Trailer at London Premiere With Blue Carpet, Splashy Piccadilly Lights Takeover ‘A Matter of Life and Death’ film still, courtesy of Front Row When the mythology behind Hayat’s curse is revealed, live-action briefly gives way to a handcrafted, gothic animated sequence. A Matter of Life and Death received its world premiere at the Red Sea International Film Festival in December 2025, before opening theatrically across Saudi Arabia in late June 25. A Matter of Life and Death was produced by Mohamed Hefzy for Film Clinic, Gianluca Chakra for Front Row Filmed Entertainment, and Abdulelah Alahmary and Ahmad Taema for Arabia Pictures, with support from the Red Sea Fund. Saudi Arabia has never been nominated for the international Oscar. The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences will unveil the 15 films on the best international feature film shortlist on Dec. 15. The five nominees will be announced Jan. 21, 2027. The 99th Academy Awards ceremony will take place on March 14, 2027. THR

title: Miami Film Festival GEMS Sets Lineup With ‘The Debut,’ ‘Club Kid’ as Opening and Closing Titles
full_text: Oct 7, 2026 9:00am PT Miami Film Festival GEMS Sets Lineup With ‘The Debut,’ ‘Club Kid’ as Opening and Closing Titles By Jordan Moreau Plus Icon Jordan Moreau Latest ‘The Social Reckoning’ First Reactions: A ‘Solid Sequel,’ ‘Good, Just Not Great Film’ and a ‘Harsh Assessment of Zuckerberg’ 2 days ago ‘Free Elizabeth Holmes’ Group Defends Convicted Theranos Founder at ‘You Can See Everything’ Doc Screening: She’s ‘Innocent and Needs to Be Free’ 2 days ago ‘Lanterns’ Finale: Hal Jordan’s Killer and Manhunter Revealed, Sinestro Creates [SPOILER], John Stewart Powers Up for ‘Superman’ Sequel 3 days ago See All A24 Miami Dade College’s Miami Film Festival unveiled the lineup for its 13th Miami Film Festival GEMS, the festival’s fall midseason event taking place from Oct. 29-Nov. 5. GEMS will open with A24’s “The Debut” from writer-director Jesse Eisenberg and close with A24’s “ Club Kid ” from writer-director and star Jordan Firstman. Julianne Moore stars in “The Debut” as Mona Friedman, a shy, unassuming housewife who is cast in a bit part at a small community theater and becomes a zealous method actor, ready to wage war on the show’s domineering director (Paul Giamatti) to protect the artistic integrity of her role. The musical comedy also stars Halle Bailey, Eisenberg and Bernadette Peters, with music and lyrics by Eisenberg. Related Stories Lego's 'Heartlake the Musical' Heads to Peacock in the U.S., Tencent in China Amid Global Sales (EXCLUSIVE) Disney Licenses Slew of Titles to Netflix, Including All Five 'Ice Age' Movies, 'Percy Jackson and the Olympians,' 'Felicity,' 'Will Trent,' 'Elio' and More (EXCLUSIVE) In “Club Kid,” Firstman stars as Peter, a hard-partying New York City club promoter whose whirlwind lifestyle is upended by the arrival of the 10-year-old son he never knew he had. The film, which had its world premiere in Un Certain Regard at the Cannes Film Festival, also stars Cara Delevingne, Diego Calva and Kirby Howell-Baptiste. Popular on Variety Centerpiece titles include “Being Heumann”, “Behemoth!”, “Bunker”, “Elsinore”, “Paper Tiger”, and “Wild Horse Nine.” The festival also places a focus on international submissions to the Academy Awards, and will feature submitted titles such as Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s “All of a Sudden”, Lukas Dhont’s “Coward”, and Andrey Zvyagintsev’s “Minotaur.” Variety will also honor Emmy Award-winning and Golden Globe-nominated actor, writer and director actor John Turturro with the Variety Creative Vanguard Award during the festival. The award will be presented as part of a moderated conversation about his illustrious career and his latest film, “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York”, hosted by Variety’s co-president and co-editor-in-chief Ramin Setoodeh. “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York,” written and directed by Noah Segan, will also screen at the festival. Additionally, “Mouse,” from directors Kelly O’Sullivan and Alex Thompson, will screen as part of the lineup, with the filmmakers receiving the Festival’s Art of Light Award. The film premiered at the Berlin International Film Festival and comes from the filmmakers behind “Ghostlight.” Kyle MacLachlan will receive the Precious Gem Award at a special event in partnership with Books & Books in Miami to honor the release of his debut memoir “Fictional Self.” In honor of the 25th anniversary of “Hedwig and the Angry Inch,” the festival will host a special retrospective screening of the cult-favorite rock musical, followed by the Impact Award presentation and Q&A with writer, director and star John Cameron Mitchell. “The 13th edition of GEMS further solidifies the festival as a major awards season stop, bringing together some of the most anticipated films of the year alongside a curated collection of discoveries from around the world,” said Lauren Cohen, Director of Programming. “With 50 titles, this is the largest GEMS line-up yet. To be able to celebrate the work of incredible storytellers such as Danny Boyle, Martin McDonagh, James Gray, Pedro Almodovar, Ryusuke Hamaguchi, Hirokazu Kore-eda, Mike Leigh, Siân Heder, and Brad Bird all in one lineup captures the richness and resonance of world cinema today.” “Audiences can expect GEMS 2026 to be one of our most memorable editions yet,” said James Woolley, Executive Director of the festival. “We are beyond thrilled to honor actor Kyle MacLachlan, filmmaker John Cameron Mitchell and Los Javis for their incredible contributions to the entertainment industry.” The Centerpiece films include: “Being Heumann” – from Academy Award-winning director Siân Heder, who co-wrote the screenplay with Rebekah Taussig, is based on the memoir by disability rights activist Judy Heumann. The film tells the story of the 1977 takeover of the San Francisco Federal Building, when Heumann (Ruth Madeley) and a coalition of disabled activists refused to leave until the government enforced Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, in what became the longest occupation of a federal building in American history. Mark Ruffalo stars as Joseph Califano, the government official standing in their way, and Dylan O’Brien also stars. “Behemoth!” – From Academy Award-nominated director/writer Tony Gilroy follows Alex Serian (Pedro Pascal), a gifted cellist who returns home to Los Angeles after 20 years on the road. Music, which has been the constant all-consuming river of his life, swells him into an adventure that will change him forever. The film also stars Olivia Wilde, Eva Victor, Alexa Swinton, Kaya Ralls, Erik Griffin, JoBeth Williams, Margarita Levieva, with Hank Azaria, and Will Arnett. “Bunker” – From director Florian Zeller (“The Father,” “The Son”) Bunker centers on an architect who takes a morally ambiguous job building a survivalist bunker for a tech billionaire, while his wife begins to question their marriage of 17 years. The psychological thriller stars Javier Bardem and Penélope Cruz. “Elsinore” – From director Simon Stone (“The Dig”) and writer Stephen Beresford (“Pride”) tells the true story of actor Ian Charleson (Andrew Scott), who in 1989 stepped into the role of Hamlet at London’s National Theatre while privately battling AIDS, in a performance that became the triumph of his career. The film also stars Olivia Colman, Billie Piper and Johnny Flynn. “Paper Tiger” – In James Gray’s deeply felt and intense crime thriller, set in 1986 New York, a naïve engineer, Irwin (Miles Teller) accepts a seemingly lucrative business proposition from his brother, Gary (Adam Driver), a former cop. But when Irwin witnesses something he wasn’t meant to see at the Gowanus Canal, the brothers find themselves pulled into a dangerous confrontation with the newly emerging Russian mafia. As the threat of violence escalates, Irwin’s wife Hester (Scarlett Johansson) sounds the alarm, Irwin desperately tries to protect his family, and Gary is forced to make an impossible choice to save those he loves. “Wild Horse Nine” – From Academy Award-winning writer-director Martin McDonagh is set shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, when CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) are dispatched by their bureau chief (Steve Buscemi) from Santiago to Easter Island, where Chris’s bond with a pair of rebellious students threatens to send the trip sideways. The black comedy also stars Mariana di Girolamo, Ailín Salas with Tom Waits and Parker Posey. Two more anniversary screenings round out the program. The festival will host a special 20th anniversary screening of Sofia Coppola’s “Marie Antoinette” at Vizcaya Museum & Gardens. The festival will also present a 10th anniversary screening of Anna Biller’s “The Love Witch” in 35mm on Halloween. The festival will also host two preview night screenings before the festival dates. First will be “ Fjord ” directed by Cristian Mungiu, which will play on October 14 at Silverspot Cinema. Winner of the Palme d’Or at this year’s Cannes Film Festival, the film stars Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve. The second Preview Night title is Sundance hit Wicker directed by Alex Huston Fischer & Eleanor Wilson on October 20. The film stars Alexander Skarsgård, Olivia Colman, Elizabeth Debicki, Peter Dinklage & Richard E. Grant. The drama series originally debuted on the basic cabler on Aug. 7, with the Season 1 finale set to air on Oct. 9. The show is based on Nevada Barr’s Anna Pigeon book series. “It’s been really thrilling to see audiences fall in love with Anna and come to the park every week,” said series showrunner Morwyn Brebner. “We’re so grateful to our cast and crew who brought Nevada Barr’s iconic world to life with such heart and passion; we cannot wait to get back outside for season two.” Related Stories Netflix Orders Dark Comedy 'All the Rage' From 'Dead to Me' Duo Liz Feldman, Kelly Hutchinson Alfonso Cuaron to Make First Korea Visit at Busan as Festival Also Spotlights European Women+ Filmmakers The series stars Tracy Spiridakos as Anna Pigeon, along with Paulina Alexis, Ronnie Rowe, Tricia Helfer, Kim Coates, Crystle Lightning, Cooper Levy, Manuel Rodriguez-Saenz, Ryan Northcott, Nikki Rae Hallow, Jordan Sledz, and Melanie Scrofano. Popular on Variety The Season 1 logline states that the show follows Pigeon, “a former city slicker who became a park ranger after a devastating loss changed the trajectory of her life forever. While Anna tries to outrun her demons, her focus turns to solving crimes that have taken place within national park grounds, no matter who or what gets in her way. Season two promises continued mystery and adventure, as Anna’s story continues to unfold.” Brebner serves as showrunner, with Lea Thompson directing. Both are also executive producers alongside Brett Burlock, Sonia Hosko, Todd Berger, Julie Di Cresce, Tom Cox, Jordy Randall, Peter Emerson and Gordon Gilbertson. Leslie Cowan serves as producer. The series is produced by Cineflix and SEVEN24 Films for USA Network in association with Bell Media. Cineflix Rights is the exclusive international worldwide distribution partner, excluding the US. “’Anna Pigeon’ has connected with audiences in a meaningful way, bringing a compelling new heroine and a fresh perspective to USA Network,” said Michael Sluchan, SVP of Scripted Content, Entertainment, at Versant. “We’re thrilled to continue Anna’s journey with Tracy, Morwyn, Lea and our incredible partners at Cineflix.” “Anna Pigeon” is one of two scripted series currently airing on USA Network. The network also has Season 2 of the legal drama “The Rainmaker,” which is based on the John Grisham novel of the same name, set to debut on Oct. 16. USA Network has also greenlit the medical drama “Diplomatic Immunity” from Matt Corman and Chris Ord. USA Network was one of the cable channels spun off into the standalone company Versant by Comcast in early 2026. Other channels now under Versant include MS Now (formerly MSNBC), E!, Syfy, and Oxygen. title: Oscars: Saudi Arabia Picks Quirky Comedy ‘A Matter of Life and Death’ for International Feature Race
full_text: Oct 7, 2026 9:00am PT Oscars: Saudi Arabia Picks Quirky Comedy ‘A Matter of Life and Death’ for International Feature Race By Nick Vivarelli Plus Icon Nick Vivarelli International Correspondent @NickVivarelli Latest ‘All’s Fair’ Season 2 to Launch From Rome Film Festival With Kim Kardashian, Naomi Watts, Niecy Nash-Betts and Sarah Paulson Attending 1 day ago Oscars: Syria Selects Doc ‘The Other Side of the Sun’ for International Feature Race, Marking First Entry Since Fall of Assad Regime 2 days ago ‘NAZA’ Rebuttal Doc Surfaces Online, Made by IDF Reserve Members 2 days ago See All Courtesy Front Row Filmed Entertainment Saudi director Anas Ba Tahaf’s romantic black comedy “A Matter of Life and Death” has been selected as Saudi Arabia ’s candidate for the Oscars international feature film category. The quirky movie marks the directorial debut of Tahaf, who previously worked as co-producer, editor and first assistant director on Mahmoud Sabbagh’s groundbreaking rom-com “Barakah Meets Barakah,” which represented Saudi Arabia at 89th Academy Awards a decade ago. Related Stories ‘Sweet Magnolias’ Cancellation: Creator, Stars JoAnna Garcia Swisher and Jamie Lynn Spears React to Netflix Series Ending Lego's 'Heartlake the Musical' Heads to Peacock in the U.S., Tencent in China Amid Global Sales (EXCLUSIVE) “A Matter of Life and Death” pairs actors Sarah Taibah (“Mandoob”) and Yaqoub Alfarhan (“Norah,” “Rashash”) and is set in Jeddah, the city on the eastern shore of the Red Sea known for vibrant youth culture, a mix of modern and ancient architecture and for being the gateway to Mecca. Popular on Variety The film’s plot involves a superstitious young woman named Hayat who is convinced she’s cursed and wants to end her life. She intersects with Yousef, an introverted heart surgeon who suffers from slower than average heartbeats that seem to quicken when he comes close to death or to killing. “She wants to die; he wants to kill, and they should be perfect for each other. Then, inconveniently, they fall in love,” says the synopsis. “A Matter of Life and Death” had its world premiere at the Red Sea International Film Festival in Jeddah in December last year, then opened theatrically in June across Saudi Arabia where it pulled a decent roughly $600,000 in grosses, according to Rentrack. The indie film later received a jury special mention at the Saudi Film Festival, where Taibah won an acting award for her performance as Hayat. “A Matter of Life and Death” is produced by Mohamed Hefzy for Film Clinic, Gianluca Chakra for Front Row Filmed Entertainment , and Abdulelah Alahmary and Ahmad Taema for Arabia Pictures, with support from the Red Sea Fund. Front Row Filmed Entertainment is handling international sales. The shortlist for the 2027 Oscar nominations will be announced by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences on Dec. 15, with the final selection revealed on Jan. 21. The 99th Academy Awards ceremony is scheduled to take place on March 14 in Los Angeles. full_text: Oct 7, 2026 9:00am PT Laika’s ‘Wildwood’ Set to Close Animation Is Film Festival By Mya Copeland Plus Icon Mya Copeland Latest Prime Video Debuts First Look at ‘Bloodaxe’ Series From ‘Vikings’ Creator (TV News Roundup) 2 days ago ‘Coven Academy’ Star Malina Weissman Unpacks Briar’s Backstory, Her Take on the Love Triangle and Her Hopes for Season 2 2 days ago ‘Celebrity Traitors’ Star Richard E. Grant Accidentally Reveals He’s a Traitor to Cast in Premiere, Calls It the ‘Biggest Mistake I’ve Made in My Life’ 5 days ago See All Laika “ Wildwood ” has been set as the closing night film for the Animation Is Film Festival , which runs Oct. 16-19 in Los Angeles. Laika’s animated epic will screen Oct. 19 at the Academy Museum’s Geffen Theater. Following the screening, “Wildwood” director and Laika president and CEO Travis Knight will hold a conversation with filmmaker Jason Reitman. “Wildwood” follows headstrong teenager Prue McKeel (Peyton Elizabeth Lee) on a desperate mission to rescue her brother after he is abducted by a murder of crows. Her rescue takes her into the Impassable Wilderness, an enchanted forest hidden just beyond Portland, Oregon. Joining Prue is her classmate Curtis Mehlberg (Jacob Tremblay), and the two enter a world of talking animals, bandits and powerful figures driven by grief and ambition. As the pair is drawn into a conflict threatening the balance of the forest itself, Prue must find a way to save her brother while confronting forces that could determine Wildwood’s future. Season 2 promises continued mystery and adventure, as Anna’s story continues to unfold. title: ‘The Hunting Wives’ Renewed For Season 3 By Netflix Ahead Of Season 2 Release
full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Skydance CEOs Meet The Press On Day One Post-Merger With String Of Promises & Few Answers Skydance Co-CEO On Prospect Of TV Studios Merging: “We’re Not Looking To Reduce Output Production” Skydance To Make Paramount & Warner Bros Lots Specialized, Each Housing Film Or TV/Streaming View All October 7, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: Malin Åkerman and Brittany Snow in 'The Hunting Wives' Netflix The frisky wives of Maple Brook will keep hunting. Netflix has given an early Season 3 renewal to The Hunting Wives , its raunchy mystery drama series starring Brittany Snow and Malin Åkerman. Casting for the eight-episode new installment is already underway. The pickup comes a month and a half ahead of the Season 2 release November 26 as a Netflix-branded series from Lionsgate Television and 3 Arts Entertainment in nearly all countries where Netflix is available. Related Stories News ‘The Hunting Wives’ Season 2 First Look Photos & Premiere Date Set At Netflix News Why Is ‘The Hunting Wives’ So Racy? Behind Netflix Series’ Unusual Deal As It Eyes UK Release & Hopes For Season 2 After Strong US Debut The unusual qualifier stems from The Hunting Wives ‘ unusual origin as a U.S.-only acquisition by Netflix of the finished first season, which had been developed and produced for Starz before reverting back to the studio in the network’s split from Lionsgate. Watch on Deadline Despite being only available in the U.S., The Hunting Wives Season 1 spent five total weeks in Netflix’s Global Top 10 English-language TV list, reaching as high as No. 2 in its second week. In light of the success, Netflix made a deal with Lionsgate, which was able to buy the show back in most international markets it had sold it to, making it available on Netflix where it made the Top 10 TV list in 40 countries, reached No. 1 in 10 countries, including the US, and has garnered over 35 million views since its July 2025 release. Once the vast majority of markets were cleared, Netflix also renewed the series created by Rebecca Cutter based on the bestselling novel by May Cobb for a second season. While Season 1 remains an acquisition, starting with Season 2, The Hunting Wives is a Netflix original. The early Season 3 renewal will allow it to return within a year, an early cadence that is increasingly becoming the standard for streamers on shows that do not require elaborate production and post-production. “I’m so stoked to be heading back to Maple Brook, and I promise that once you’ve finished Season 2, you’ll be desperate to see what happens next,” said writer, executive producer and showrunner Cutter. “Buckle up, because Season 3 will be even more scandalous and twisted.” Also executive producing are Erwin Stoff for 3 Arts Entertainment and Cobb. Lionsgate Television is the studio. full_text: Skip to main content By Rosy Cordero Rosy Cordero Associate Editor, TV @SocialRosy More Stories By Rosy André Holland Joins Universal’s ‘Miami Vice ’85’ Peri Gilpin To Play Brooke Shields’ Sister In Acorn TV’s ‘You’re Killing Me’ ‘Tulsa King’ Renewed For Season 5 With Move To NY; Scarlet Rose Stallone Promoted & Erik Palladino Among New Cast View All October 7, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L to R: Michael Irby and Gregory Sierra as Lt. Lou Rodriguez in 'Miami Vice' TV Series Getty, Universal TV EXCLUSIVE: The cast of Universal’s Miami Vice ’85 continues to expand with Michael Irby ( Mayans M.C., Barry) joining the fold. Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler lead the film as Ricardo Tubbs and Sonny Crockett, respectively. Alden Ehrenreich , Whitney Peak , Camila Morrone , John Leguizamo , Danny Ramirez and Walton Goggins also star. Irby will play Lt. Lou Rodriguez, sources close to production reveal. The original character in the hit NBC series Miami Vic e, who was boss of Metro-Dade Police Department’s Organized Crime Bureau, Vice Division, was played by Gregory Sierra. Rodriguez was killed off after four episodes at Sierra’s request to be written out because he didn’t want to move to Miami. His exit made way for Edward James Olmos to take the reins as Lt. Martin Castillo, beginning in Episode 6 of the crime drama’s freshman season. Watch on Deadline Related Stories Casting André Holland Joins Universal's 'Miami Vice '85' Casting Walton Goggins Joins Michael B. Jordan And Austin Butler In 'Miami Vice '85' At Universal The feature puts Irby on the opposite side of the law from his roles in FX’s Mayans M.C. and HBO’s Barry , where he played President of the Mayans Motor Cycle Club Obispo “Bishop” Losa and Bolivian mob boss Cristobal Sifuentes, respectively. Gregory Sierra with Philip Michael Thomas as Ricardo Tubbs and Don Johnson as Sonny Crockett in ‘Miami Vice’ pilot Universal Television From screenwriter Dan Gilroy and director Joseph Kosinski, Miami Vice ’85 explores the glamour and corruption of mid-1980s Miami in an all-new version of Miami Vice . The film is inspired by the pilot episode of the 1984-90 NBC series, titled “Brother’s Keeper,” which aired on September 16, 1984. Written by series creator Anthony Yerkovich and executive produced by Michael Mann, the two-hour series premiere of Miami Vice introduced the world to Vice cop Sonny Crockett (Don Johnson) and New York detective Ricardo Tubbs (Philip Michael Thomas), who are brought together by destiny, though they do not really vibe at first. They eventually become partners, but first they investigate Colombian drug lord Calderone (Miguel Piñero), the show’s main antagonist across Season 1. In the episode, it’s revealed why Crockett and Tubbs have beef that runs deep with Calderone. For Tubbs, he’s visiting SoFla seeking revenge for his slain brother, who was taken down after the cartel leader put out a hit on his life. Crockett also has reason to want Calderone off the streets: the crime boss killed the former’s partner Eddie Rivera (Jimmy Smits) early in the pilot. Despite first appearances, Crockett and Tubbs decide they want to work together, taking down bad guys in the Magic City and having some fun in between. Aside from the Crockett and Tubbs intro, the episode is famously known for a driving scene where the duo is in Crockett’s black Ferrari Daytona Spyder while listening to Phil Collins’ song In the Air Tonight . Also notable, though not from this episode, Leguizamo portrayed Calderone’s son Orlando twice in the series. Leguizamo will also star in Miami Vice ’85 , though it is as yet unknown if he will reprise the role. The movie will be filmed for Imax and is set for release on May 19, 2028. Production will begin this year. Miami Vice ’85 is being produced by Dylan Clark/Dylan Clark Productions ( The Batman , The Penguin ) and Kosinski ( F1 ). Gilroy is writing the script, based on characters created by Yerkovich from the series executive produced by Yerkovich and Mann. Eric Warren Singer wrote an earlier draft of the screenplay. Irby is represented by Independent Artist Group and Coronel Group. title: Oscars: Saudi Arabia Submits ‘A Matter Of Life & Death’ For Best International Feature Film
full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Low Light Films Boards Jane Schoenbrun EP’d ‘The Arrow At Rest’ + First Clip The Coven Boards Australian Slasher ‘The Only One’ Starring Mel Jarnson & Saphira Moran ‘Lucy Lost’ & ‘Submarine Jim’ Animation Studio Xilam Sets Management Reshuffle View All October 7, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'A Matter of Life and Death' Film Clinic, Front Row Productions, Arabia Pictures Group, Rotana Studios The Saudi Film Commission has selected Anas Ba Tahaf’s A Matter of Life and Death as Saudi Arabia ’s official submission for Best International Feature Film at the 99th Academy Awards. Local stars Yaqoub Alfarhan ( Scales , Norah ) and Sarah Taibah ( Mandoob ) play an unlikely couple whose love blossoms against the odds in the Jeddah-set feature, one of the quirkiest local romantic-come-black comedies to come out of Saudi Arabia since the lifting of its 35-year cinema ban in 2017. Related Stories News Oscars 2027 International Feature Film Submissions By Country: Denmark, Italy & Spain Among Latest To Declare Below The Line 2026-27 Awards Season Calendar: Oscars, Emmys, Grammys, Guilds & More Taibah, who also wrote the screenplay, plays Hayat, a fiercely independent young woman convinced that a generational curse will kill her on her 30th birthday. Having made peace with dying, she crosses paths with Yousef (Alfarhan), a brilliant but emotionally detached heart surgeon living with bradycardia. His abnormally slow heartbeat only seems to quicken when he comes close to death or to killing. As a surgeon surrounded every day by the fragile line between life and death, temptation is never far away. She wants to die, he wants to kill, and they should be perfect for each other. Then, inconveniently, they fall in love. Watch on Deadline The cast also features Hosam Al Harthy, Fay Fouad, Amani Aljameel, Ghada Aboud, Rahaf Ibrahim and Najla Alabdullah, with production design by Ibrahim Khorma. The film world premiered at the Red Sea International Film Festival in December 2025, before opening theatrically across Saudi Arabia on June 25, 2026 . It later received a Jury Special Mention at the 12th Saudi Film Festival, where Taibah won the Golden Palm for Best Acting for her performance as Hayat. Director Ba Tahaf previously worked as coproducer, editor and first assistant director on Mahmoud Sabbagh’s Barakah Meets Barakah , which represented Saudi Arabia in the Best Foreign Language Film category at the 89th Academy Awards. A Matter of Life and Death is produced by Mohamed Hefzy for Film Clinic , Gianluca Chakra for Front Row Filmed Entertainment, and Abdulelah Alahmary and Ahmad Taema for Arabia Pictures, with support from the Red Sea Fund. Front Row Filmed Entertainment is handling international sales. “Hayat is impulsive, funny, stubborn, fearless and spectacularly headstrong, a contemporary Saudi woman written without explanation or apology. Her independence is not the story. It is simply who she is,” wrote Front Row in a statement announcing the Saudi Oscar entry. “The film’s originality lies as much in how it is told as in its premise. Its heightened visual style moves confidently between romance, fantasy and black comedy, shifting tone without settling neatly into any one genre. When the mythology behind Hayat’s curse is revealed, live action briefly gives way to a handcrafted, gothic animated sequence, adding another unexpected layer to the film’s visual language.” “Together, these elements give A Matter of Life and Death an identity that stands apart within Saudi cinema and feels equally distinctive within Arab filmmaking more broadly. Set and shot in Jeddah, the city is integral to that identity. Its streets, architecture, humour, language and contradictions are woven into the story, grounding its increasingly fantastical world in a recognisable contemporary reality.” Written by and starring Sarah Taibah alongside Yaqoub Al Farhan, the film is produced by Film Clinic, Front Row Filmed Entertainment and Arabia Pictures, with Front Row handling international sales. Saudi Arabia, which first started submitting films to the Oscars in 2013, kicking off with Haifaa Al-Mansour’s Wadjada. Subsequent entries have included Barakah Meets Barakah (2016) and Shahad Ameen’s Hijra last year. The country has yet to be nominated. title: In a Groundbreaking Premium Drama, ‘R91’ Brings a Murder Mystery Aboard Flagship French Aircraft Carrier
full_text: Oct 7, 2026 8:58am PT In a Groundbreaking Premium Drama, ‘R91’ Brings a Murder Mystery Aboard Flagship French Aircraft Carrier In this fictional 6-part drama brought to market at Mipcom by SND, France's R91 Charles de Gaulle becomes the setting of a gritty, realistic thriller powered by M6 and Prime Video, produced by Next Episode (UGC Group) and born out of the mind of co-creator, co-writer and producer Henri Debeurme By Kevin Giraud Plus Icon Kevin Giraud Latest BBC, Bobby Prod, Folivari, Gao Shan Pictures Honored by Europe’s Animation Industry at Cartoon Forum 3 weeks ago Upcoming Canadian Animated Series Shine At Cartoon Forum 2026 3 weeks ago Heartfelt, Rare Animated Belgian Feature ‘Juul’ Headlines Studio 100 Film’s Expanding Slate at TIFF Market 3 weeks ago See All 'R91' Courtesy of SND Mediterranean Sea, present day. France’s nuclear aircraft carrier R91 – Charles de Gaulle aka “Le Charles” has just set sail on a threat-assessment strategic mission. When a crew member is found dead and another goes missing, military investigator Paul Fischer (Alban Lenoir, “Lost Bullet”) is rushed aboard. With second-in-command Helena Duval (Elodie Yung, “Marvel’s Daredevil,” “The Cleaning Lady”), they must hunt for the truth before the killer strikes again in the dark corners of the floating fortress. Related Stories 'Angus, Thongs and Full-Frontal Snogging' Pilot Set at Netflix Pam Levine Exits Netflix as Marketing & Publicity VP (EXCLUSIVE) With 2,000 souls on board, the stakes are high and suspicion spreads, as the mission turned murder investigation slowly transforms into a global security crisis. Popular on Variety Henri Debeurme, co-creator, co-writer, producer of ‘R91’. Credits Fanta Kaba A Series Mania winner “R91” marks the first ever co-acquisition between Amazon Prime Video France and leading free-to-air network M6 , with international sales handled by SND . It was born at the Cannes Film Festival in 2024, as producer, co-creator and co-writer Henri Debeurme at Next Episode Productions, part of UGC Group, exited the world premiere of “Top Gun: Maverick.” As he recalls to Variety ahead of the series’ own world premiere in La Rochelle Fiction Festival , his childhood desire to make such high-end productions in France was triggered once again by the Top Gun’s striking imagery, and by a chance encounter with Brigitte Maccioni, CEO of UGC Group. Maccioni, who had been part of the French Navy citizen reserve, had worked on “Le Charles” and met a few people during her time aboard the ship. “She opened a crack in the door for me, and when you find doors like that, you have to push and open them,” recalls Debeurme. “And that gave me the impetus to imagine a series that could take place on an aircraft carrier such as the Charles de Gaulle.” However, the seasoned creative took his time, building his script with co-writers, co-creators Mathilde Arnaud and Yoann Legave, and discussing with broadcasters and partners at M6, UGC and Prime Video. “The first constraint of such an endeavor is a narrative one,” he explains. “Writing a story set on a warship brings specific challenges, as you have to find plot twists within this defined setting. Series set entirely in a single location are not that common, and they’re often relying on claustrophobia to add tension, such as submarine series or family dramas.” He adds: “With ‘R91,’ we tried something new. A spectacular, closed-room drama also opened to the outside world. Ultimately, the aircraft carrier setting was more of an advantage than an restraint, as we discovered it to be a true floating village, open to the outside world, the sea and the sky. It became a source of ideas, inspiration, and unexpected turns.” Even though “R91” is entirely fictional, the teams wanted credibility and authenticity. And with the ambition of shooting almost the entire series at sea, it was key to have the French Navy on board. Debeurme approached them after refining his concept with his teams and broadcasting partners, and the Navy authorities eventually proved easy to convince. “They were welcoming, without willing to control us in any way. It was accompaniment during the whole process, as long as we didn’t interfere with their actual daily jobs.” With that in mind, Debeurme and his teams set out to build the most intricate, complex shooting schedule he’s ever created. “We had authorization to board the ships during military exercises, and we filmed for 15 days at sea, notably on the Charles, on the sole condition we didn’t disrupt their movements, and that we brought everything we needed with us. The preexisting exercises we joined, such as bridging and catapult launches, were planned a long time before, and we had to match their schedule.” Schedules that would change on a daily basis. By the end of shooting, not a single day had gone as planned, adds Debeurme. “We basically had to film a complex, fictional series as we would a documentary, doing a 10-minute take out of the blue because an helicopter is landing, and we want actors to be getting out of it, or saying their lines in front of it. Sometimes, we’d have to shoot with aircrafts landing or being launched on top of us, which makes tremendous noise. To be honest, it was completely insane and ended up being the most complicated shooting I’ve ever done in my entire career. We had to constantly adapt.” These conditions eventually bonded the teams, as well as helped them connect with the sailors themselves. “Their flexibility and open-mindedness helped us and made us feel like we were fully immersed. In some ways, film crews and navy crews share similarities. Both are very ordered collectives where everyone is an expert in their field, and we all are equally passionate about our jobs.” Using generative AI or stock footage was never Debeurme’s intention. “We filmed on different ships and also built sets in a studio for locations that were too cramped, inaccessible or too complex for VFX. But the vast majority took place on real warships, with working sailors. We wanted to film real people, real things. This authenticity was always at the core of our process, and that involves humans. French, world-class talents and artists that helped us bring this project to life with a fraction of the budget of U.S. dramas.” Expanding on French drama series, Debeurme praised his colleagues and fellow artists presenting audacious, imaginative projects in La Rochelle. “Throughout my career, I’ve had many projects where people told me it was something that could be done only in the US. ‘A series set on an aircraft carrier? No, we are terrible at that,’ people would say. But I actually disagree. I think we have exceptional teams in France, powerful imagination and a wealthy pool of talent, and we shouldn’t be afraid to try new things.” “R91” showcases this boldness, which shone also in La Rochelle with premium period dramas such as “Swapped,” unique in its own way. As he heads to the festival, Debeurme is incredibly thankful for all who helped bring this crazy dream project to life. “It’s a huge source of pride, and a childhood dream of mine. And for me, it still is all about movies and TV series that make my dreams come true. As a writer-producer on this show, I’m glad to see I could pull off such an ambitious project, and that having these two roles in a European context is possible. And beyond my own experience, it also proves that we’re still in a world where, even if matters are very difficult and the industry is under a lot of pressure, you can still do great things when you use your imagination and conviction.” Following up its world premiere, “R91” will debut on Prime Video in the near future, before airing on M6. ‘Will You Still Be My Friend’ Director Lu Po-Shun on Finding Common Ground From San Sebastian to Busan Ray Panthaki Debut, Jose Maria Cabral, Frederic Baillif Pics Make the Cut at Tallinn Black Nights Official and First Films Competitions Prime Day Blu-ray Deals Include 50% Discounts on Dozens of Films and Boxed Sets: ‘Boogie Nights, ‘Pulp Fiction,’ ‘The Sopranos’ and More George Cheeks Addresses Staffers in First Memo as Skydance TV Co-Chair: ‘CBS Remains a Cornerstone’ Saoirse Ronan Responds to James Bond Rumors About Husband Jack Lowden: ‘Not Really a Subject That’s Coming Up in Our House’ Josh Goldstine to Oversee Marketing and Distribution at Warner Bros., Paramount and All Skydance Film Labels (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments...

title: ‘Satoko Always’ Review: A Trio of Women Find Their Inner Voice in Shuichi Okita’s Delightful Celebration of the Art of Writing
full_text: Oct 7, 2026 8:53am PT ‘Satoko Always’ Review: A Trio of Women Find Their Inner Voice in Shuichi Okita’s Delightful Celebration of the Art of Writing Kasumi Arimura, Hikari Ishida and young breakout Kashun Himeno play three women with the same name, who tap into their creative sides in this charming Busan competition entry. By James Marsh Plus Icon James Marsh Latest ‘The Table: Day and Night’ Review: Café-Based Korean Romance With Kim Min-ha and Han Sun-hwa Is All Froth, No Kick 18 hours ago See All Three total strangers, with nothing in common except their name, are each inspired to take up writing in “ Satoko Always ,” writer-director Shuichi Okita ’s surprising and inventive celebration of womanhood and the art of literary composition. Kasumi Arimura is the undeniable headliner, but the popular starlet is matched every step of the way by veteran actress Hikari Ishida and especially Kashun Himeno, who unleashes an eye-catching, potentially star-making turn as a junior high school student experiencing her first taste of true love. Related Stories ‘Tyson’ Trailer: Mike Tyson Chronicles His Journey From Dropout to Heavyweight Champion in Netflix Docuseries Danny Boyle Says ‘28 Years Later Part 3’ Will ‘Have a Lot of Cillian Murphy in It’ and Backs Jack O’Connell as the Next James Bond Having already debuted domestically last month, the film makes its international debut in Busan’s competition section, where it is sure to draw praise for Okita’s wonderfully woven screenplay, together with its triumvirate of stellar performances. Similarly, cast and creator’s robust reputation should likely ensure the film secures healthy distribution across Asia and select western markets. Popular on Variety Plucky teenager Satoko Nakai (Himeno) is first introduced with a nebulizer thrust up her nose. She is being treated for allergic rhinitis, which immediately becomes a non-issue when her handsome classmate Hayase (Toharu Ogawa) appears beside her, ready to be administered a similar treatment. They hit it off famously, and although Satoko is initially put off when Hayase blanks her at school, their regular sessions at the ENT clinic soon bring them closer together. Unfortunately, Satoko’s rhinitis interferes with her sleep, causing her to doze off at a kabuki performance she had been assigned to write a report on. Rather than turn in a blank paper, Satoko conjures up a work of pure fiction, which, much to her surprise, is warmly received by her teacher, Ms. Terao (Yoh Yoshida), who encourages her to indulge her passion for creative writing. She is tasked with penning a love letter to her favourite food, and the resulting ode to shiokara (fermented shrimp) is in fact a thinly veiled declaration of her blossoming adoration for Hayase. Okita’s screenplay gleefully challenges cinematic conventions, persistently playing with the viewer’s comprehension of what is actually unfolding, and what is mere fantasy, bursting from the pen of this newly inspired wordsmith. While never allowing this metatextual mischievousness to derail the narrative, these ideas flow seamlessly into the second chapter, in which thirty-something film publicist Satoko Nishida (Arimura) writes and feasts on shiokara when not indulging her passion for ludicrously romantic K-dramas. We are told this is not the same person, and yet they share so many things in common. At work, Satoko attempts to create a campaign for a new Korean baseball drama that her company is releasing, but after hours she is involved in an extramarital affair with a business associate, Muramoto (Joe Odagiri). That dalliance reaches a potentially lethal tipping point that leaves Satoko in the hospital, newly inspired to create a romantic fairytale of her own. Later still, we are introduced to Satoko Iijima (Ishida), who again shares many defining features with her two namesakes, albeit with just enough subtle differences to keep the audience on the back foot. Happily married and the mother of three boys, Satoko has been playing the dutiful housewife for years, but when her youngest, Shota (Mansaku Takada), reveals that he will be moving out when he starts university, the prospect of being an empty-nester sends her into a tailspin. She reminisces about a boy she knew growing up, and from there is inspired to create a story of her own, which the film realises through a visually dynamic combination of live-action and stop-motion animation. To reveal more of Okita’s endlessly surprising and playfully ambiguous script would be to rob audiences of the film’s numerous pleasures, which run the gamut from hearty belly-laughs to heartbreaking melodrama. The veteran storyteller, known for such surprising and rewarding works as “The Woodsman and the Rain” (2011) and “The Story of Yonosuke” (2013), not only dazzles with his dextrous interweaving of character and style, but also honors the craft of writing itself, spotlighting the texture and feel of paper, pencil and eraser. Even when his characters do use a computer screen, Okita shoots so tight on the cursor and characters, even their intricate composition appears tactile and sculpted. A film about indulging our yearning to open our hearts and tell stories, not for the entertainment of others or financial reward, but as a creative and emotional outlet to nurture one’s own sanity and well-being, “Satoko Always” cannot help but inspire the creative voice inside us all. That it is also a film about women, lifting them up without any compulsion to push men down in the process, is the final flourish in a work that achieves much with a gently assured touch. ‘Satoko Always’ Review: A Trio of Women Find Their Inner Voice in Shuichi Okita’s Delightful Celebration of the Art of Writing Reviewed at Busan Film Festival (Competition), Oct. 7, 2026. Running time: 138 min. Production: (Japan) An Amuse Creative Studio production. (World sales: Hakuhodo DY Music & Pictures, Tokyo.) Producers: Ryuhei Tsutsui, Miyuki Sato, Suguru Kubota, Yuya Tanaka. Crew: Director, screenplay: Shuichi Okita. Camera: Akiko Ashizawa. Editor: Masaya Ozaki. Music: Satoko Shibata. With: Kasumi Arimura, Hikari Ishida, Kashun Himeno, Joe Odagiri, Yoh Yoshida, Mansaku Takada, Yuzu Aoki, Michitaka Tsutsui, Toharu Ogawa, Yuko Nakamura, Kanata Hosoda. title: Grammy Predictions: It’s a Race Between Olivia and Olivia
full_text: × Skip to main content Illustration by Andrew Archer If you knew a year ago that the next 12 months would yield albums from Taylor Swift, Harry Styles and Bruno Mars, you probably would have placed your bets on Grammy nominations right then. But as the announcement of the finalists for the 2026 awards approaches, none of those juggernauts feels like frontrunners for the big prizes. Instead, the spotlight has pivoted to two 20-something women named Olivia. Those superstar releases certainly weren’t flops; Swift’s The Life of a Showgirl was the fastest-selling album of all time, and Styles is in the middle of a record-breaking 30-night stand at Madison Square Garden, while Bruno Mars spent much of the year near the top of the charts with The Romantic lead single “I Just Might.” But for three historic Grammy darlings who’ve all won album of the year over the course of the past decade, they all ultimately seemed to come up short either commercially or critically and don’t quite carry the expected enthusiasm or momentum into awards season. Related Stories Movies Actor Jack Reynor to Be Honored at the Oscar Wilde Awards (Exclusive) THR Cover Story Olivia Rodrigo: The Queen of Sad Finds Her Happy Place Bruno Mars Kevin Mazur/Getty Images As Grammy season comes into full swing, one of the biggest questions the Recording Academy will need to wrestle with is how to handle the current surge in popularity for country music. In September, for the first time ever, the top five slots on the singles chart were all held by country songs — most notably, Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas,” which recently broke the record for longest stay at No. 1. Langley seems an obvious lock for best new artist, but the academy has steered clear of Nashville when it comes to the big awards; the only “mainstream” country releases ever to win album of the year were Swift’s 2010 Fearless and Glen Campbell’s By the Time I Get to Phoenix in 1968. (Kacey Musgraves’ Golden Hour won in 2019, though that’s more of an alternative country album than a traditional country radio-friendly project.) Ella Langley Courtesy of Columbia Records Meanwhile, Morgan Wallen (whose Still the Problem Tour just became the highest-grossing country tour in history) continues to boycott the Grammys, as does Drake, whose three 2026 albums and summer anthem “Janice STFU” may otherwise have been in awards contention. Adding to this ongoing mess, BTS opted not to submit their album Arirang , protesting the addition of a new K-pop category, which they believe will hinder Korean artists’ chances for consideration for the general pop awards. So with all of those options either off the table or looking at diminished expectations, that brings us to Olivia Rodrigo and Olivia Dean . Both previous best new artist winners, both beloved across multiple genres, they’re clearly the acts in pole position in a year when it’s unlikely that any one artist is going to dominate the ceremonies. Rodrigo’s New Wave-inflected You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love tips toward younger fans and garners more of a rock following, while Dean’s The Art of Loving leans R&B with a more mature audience. Rodrigo’s album, released in June, could benefit from recency bias, coupled with the buzz around her Daisy Chain Fields Music Festival, but Dean has a case for longevity, still parked in the top 10 after a full year. Olivia Rodrigo, Noah Kahan and Olivia Dean JMEnternational/Getty Images; Joseph Okpako/WireImage; Christopher Polk/Billboard/Getty Images Both are sure things for album of the year nods, with a possible slight edge to You Seem Pretty Sad , constructed as more of a top-to-bottom “album” chronicling the beginning, middle and end of a relationship. Elsewhere in the category, British soulstress Raye’s This Music May Contain Hope wasn’t the same commercial smash, though she’s still the kind of ambitious, old-school artist that Grammy voters like — as is Noah Kahan, whose The Great Divide will get the recognition that his powerhouse Stick Season was denied. Even if Swift’s Showgirl and Bruno Mars’ The Romantic haven’t gotten the same reception as their best loved works, they still seem too big to fail and likely will get nominated. If any “legacy” artists make the cut, signs point to Madonna — whose Confessions II was widely lauded as her strongest effort in 20 years, a more compelling story than steady new albums from Paul McCartney and The Rolling Stones. At the cool kids table, Rosalía’s jaw-dropping Lux was a (deserving) critical favorite and, following last year’s win for Bad Bunny’s Debí Tirar Más Fotos , it would be a bad look not to include a Spanish-language artist. From the indie rock world, Phoebe Bridgers’ Lost Weekend is her acclaimed solo return after 2023’s seven-times-nominated, three-time Grammy-winning boygenius album The Record . Rosalía Kevin Mazur/Getty Images It was a quiet year for hip-hop, so while J. Cole’s “farewell album” The Fall-Off and Don Toliver’s Octane are remote possibilities to sneak into a nomination slot, for the Grammys, it increasingly feels like Kendrick Lamar or nothing. Musgraves’ Middle of Nowhere was considered a return to form, but if voters lean into a country project, it’s hard to imagine anything other than Langley’s Dandelion getting the nod this year. Which leaves Styles as the odd man out. If the sin of Mars’ album was being too predictable, Styles’ bold and unexpected Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally was tougher for fans and, likely, for Grammy voters; the album sunk rapidly on the charts and (despite the support that led to Harry’s House winning the album prize in 2023 over Adele, Beyoncé and Lamar) could come up short this time. Both Olivias also will feature in the record and song of the year categories, with Ms. Dean’s breezy, omnipresent “Man I Need” a favorite. It’s not clear which songs Rodrigo will submit where — maybe “Drop Dead” goes stronger as a recording and “The Cure” is a better fit for the songwriters’ award, but we shall see. Raye’s irrepressible “Where Is My Husband!” is a clear record of the year contender, and “Choosin’ Texas” feels certain to make it to the finals. Kahan’s title track, Tame Impala and Jennie’s collaboration “Vampire” and Mars’ “I Just Might” are in the running, and Sienna Spiro’s “Die on This Hill” has made her the latest U.K. pop-soul crossover (in the tradition of Amy Winehouse, Adele, etc.), a sound that consistently plays into Grammy voters’ tastes. Song of the year will offer most of the same names as the record of the year picks, though here Dean might switch her entry to “So Easy (To Fall in Love),” co-written by Grammy favorite Amy Allen. Longer shots include Styles’ “Aperture,” PinkPantheress and Zara Larsson’s “Stateside” and Brandi Carlile’s battle cry for the U.S. Constitution, “Church and State.” Then of course there’s T-Swift, who despite her legendary legacy has never won for record or song of the year. “The Fate of Ophelia” was a huge hit, spending 12 weeks at No. 1. But “I Knew It, I Knew You,” from the Toy Story 5 soundtrack, marked her return to country radio and might read as more of a “songwriter” song; when she recently did a rare interview event with Grammy CEO Harvey Mason Jr., it was the one Grammy-eligible song she performed. Taylor Swift, The Life of a Showgirl Courtesy of Mert Alaz & Marcus Piggott/TAS Rights Management The smart money says that she splits the difference, putting “The Fate of Ophelia” up for record and saving “I Knew It, I Knew You” for song. Overall, her focus seems set on winning an Oscar for “I Knew It, I Knew You,” which seems inevitable. In a year when there’s a strong chance four different women will carry away the Big Four trophies, Swift will have positioned herself to wind up, once again, as Music’s Biggest Story. This story appeared in the Oct. 7 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine.

title: David Brindley Confirmed As Channel 4 Content Chief
full_text: Skip to main content By Stewart Clarke , Jesse Whittock October 7, 2026 8:42am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Channel 4's headquarters Getty UPDATED with confirmation: David Brindley has been confirmed as the new Director of Programmes at Channel 4 . He will have oversight of all scripted and unscripted genres and will join the Channel 4 board. Channel 4 CEO Priya Dogra said Brindley “has a proven ability to nurture the ideas and talent that create truly standout television.” Related Stories News Louisa Compton Appointed To Channel 4 Board Alongside Next Content Chief News Sony Chief Wayne Garvie: “It’s Very Difficult To See How Channel 4 Survives In Present Form” “As we reshape Channel 4 to invest more in distinctive British content and back creative talent across the UK, I wanted a Director of Programmes who would be able to take ambitious risks in programming and deliver powerful shows that make a cultural impact, while sustaining the bold attitude that has always been the calling card of Channel 4,” she added. “With hundreds of hours of award-winning shows under his belt and deep experience working in public service broadcasting, David is the ideal person to join our existing creative leadership team and help us deliver our vision for the future of Channel 4.” Brindley will “work alongside” news and digital boss Louisa Compton and content strategy chief Kiran Nataraja in the new-look commissioning leadership team. Compton will also join the board . Watch on Deadline He said: “I’m immensely proud to be joining the talented team at Channel 4. At a moment of seismic change within the industry and the channel, it has never been more important to ensure Channel 4 thrives creatively, by deepening its connection with audiences and the production community across the country.” PREVIOUSLY, October 6: David Brindley is set to land one of the biggest jobs in UK television, overseeing programming at pubcaster Channel 4. He is being lined up to replace Ian Katz, who leaves this month having been the broadcaster’s longest-serving Chief Content Officer. Channel 4 declined comment. Broadcast was first with the news. Following a long interview process, Brindley, the CEO of Destination X producer Twofour, and former BBC Three boss Stuart Murphy were understood to have been the final two in the running. Brindley has been considered a frontrunner for the role since speculation began over who would replace Katz. His ITV Studios-backed outfit produces both the UK and U.S. versions of Destination X and Apple TV’s The Reluctant Traveler with Eugene Levy , and he is well-established in British unscripted production circles. Brindley previously worked for Channel 4 and was behind one of its most impactful shows of all time, Educating Yorkshire , which he recently revived at Twofour. Considered a savvy operator with commissioning and production experience, he got down to the last four for the top BBC content job last year. His competitor for the role, Murphy, would have been a more left-field choice given he has spent most of the past decade out of television. After playing major roles at the BBC, where he launched BBC Three in 2003, and Sky, where he was Director of Entertainment Channels between 2015 and 2018, he became CEO of the English National Opera in 2018 and held the role for five years. Others understood to have been in the running included BBC iPlayer boss Dan McGolpin, Amazon’s Clarkson’s Farm exec Fozia Khan and Tanya Shaw, who has run British indies Shine and Zinc. Brindley’s job is a tough one. Channel 4 is laying off around 340 staff, the net’s biggest round of cuts in its 40-year history , and this is hitting commissioning hard, with around 50% of roles set to be reduced. Big shifts he will oversee include combining the drama and comedy teams into one scripted unit and a merger of its unscripted divisions. The nature of his role has also changed since Katz left. Brindley will report to new CEO Priya Dogra, as will news boss Louisa Compton and strategy chief Kiran Nataraja. Both Brindley and Compton will sit on the Channel 4 board. Compton and Nataraja previously reported to Katz. Max Goldbart contributed reporting.
